ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, smooth parallel metal rails fixed on a horizontal plane have spacing L, the right end is connected to a resistor with resistance R, and there exists in space a uniform magnetic field with direction vertically upward and magnetic induction intensity B. A conducting rod ab with mass m and resistance r is connected to a fixed spring and placed on the rails. At the initial moment, the spring is exactly at its natural length. Give the conducting rod an initial velocity v0 horizontally to the right, and the conducting rod begins to move back and forth along the rails. During this process, the conducting rod is always perpendicular to the rails and maintains good contact. It is known that the resistance r of the conducting rod is equal to the resistance value of the fixed resistor R, and the resistance of the rails is neglected, then which of the following statements is correct (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, smooth parallel metal rails fixed on a horizontal plane have spacing L, and the right end is connected to a resistor with resistance R. There exists in space a uniform magnetic field with direction vertically upward and magnetic induction intensity B. A conducting rod ab with mass m and resistance r is connected to a fixed spring and placed on the rails. At the initial moment, the spring is exactly at its natural length. After giving the conducting rod an initial velocity v0 horizontally to the right, the conducting rod begins to move back and forth along the rails. It is known that r=R, and the resistance of the rails is neglected. At the initial moment when the conducting rod begins to move, what is the direction of the Ampere force it receives?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there are two horizontal parallel metal rails, whose right ends are connected by resistor R to form a closed loop; the conducting rod ab is placed vertically between the upper and lower rails and is connected to the fixed spring on the left side; beside the rod there is an initial-velocity arrow v0, directed horizontally to the right; dot-like magnetic-field symbols are distributed in the rail region, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the rail plane upward. Then reason: initially the spring is at its natural length; after the conducting rod obtains a rightward velocity, it cuts magnetic induction lines, and an induced current is produced in the closed loop. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic effect produced by the induced current should hinder the relative motion that causes the induced current, namely hinder the conducting rod from moving to the right. Therefore the direction of the Ampere force initially received by the conducting rod is opposite to the direction of the initial velocity, and is to the left.
